html:
The Borgu States were a group of kingdoms of the Bariba (Baatombu) and Boko peoples on both sides of today's border between Benin and Nigeria, west of the middle Niger. The map shows them in 1880 and 1900. The main ones were Bussa, Nikki, Kaiama and Illo.

They were ruled by a warrior aristocracy of horsemen, the Wasangari, and were known for resisting their neighbours. Borgu stood off the powerful Yoruba empire of Oyo at times, and it was never conquered by the jihad of the Sokoto Caliphate.

The Scottish explorer Mungo Park drowned in the Niger rapids at Bussa in 1806. In the 1890s Britain and France raced to sign treaties with Borgu's rulers, and in 1898 they split it, the west going to French Dahomey and the east to British Nigeria.
